te.name: Special September Teal Zone
te.bounds: The Special September Teal Zone is the area south of the C&D Canal to north of Route 9 in Lewes and east of Routes 13, 113/113A and 1. The line is DNREC’s own Teal Zone map, which runs on Route 1 (not Route 113) south of Dover; across the bay the app carries it due east from the C&D Canal mouth and from Lewes to the state line (approximate).
te.note: September teal Sept 5–13 here only. Resident Canada geese Sept 1–25, with special methods (unplugged guns, electronic calls, to half an hour after sunset) allowed only Sept 1–4 and Sept 14–25. Every other season is statewide.

st.name: Rest of Delaware
st.bounds: All of Delaware outside the Special September Teal Zone.
st.note: No September teal season. Every other season is statewide.

seasonsNote: Delaware allows Sunday waterfowl hunting during the seasons on private land (with permission) and on designated public land.

seasons.label: Sea ducks
seasons.note: Delaware no longer has a special sea duck zone — sea ducks follow the duck season, 4 a day inside the 6.

seasons.label: Canada geese — early
seasons.note: Resident Canada geese. In the Teal Zone special methods are not allowed Sept 5–13. Shooting to half an hour after sunset only with special methods.

seasons.label: Canada geese — regular
seasons.note: Migratory Canada geese, white-fronted geese included.

seasons.label: Snow geese
seasons.note: Snow and Ross’s geese. DNREC lists Feb 1–5 and Feb 6 – Mar 10 after Jan 31; the eRegulations guide lists Feb 1–6 and Feb 8 – Mar 10 — check DNREC about Feb 7. No conservation order in 2027 (DNREC).

seasons.label: Tundra swan (permit)
seasons.note: By lottery permit only (up to 272 permits; applications closed Sept 15). Mute swans may be taken in any open waterfowl season.

seasons.label: Crows
seasons.note: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays only (the season opened July 3, 2026; a June 24–27, 2027 segment follows).

bags.detail: Six ducks a day (mergansers and coots apart), inside which the species limits below apply. Possession three times the daily limit.
Any species in the aggregate; no separate hooded merganser limit.
Inside the 6: no more than 3 scoters, 3 eiders (1 hen), 3 long-tailed ducks.
Migratory Canada geese, white-fronted geese included.
Tundra swan, by permit. Mute swans: no limit.
Sora and Virginia rails, singly or in the aggregate.
King and clapper rails, singly or in the aggregate.

duckSublimits.note: no more than 3 scoters, 3 eiders (1 hen), 3 long-tailed ducks
teal, shoveler, gadwall, wigeon, goldeneye, ring-necked, bufflehead, ruddy — up to the full bag

rules.d: State law allows Sunday hunting for waterfowl during the seasons on private land (with the landowner’s permission) and on designated public land.
One-half hour before sunrise to sunset for all migratory birds and mute swans. September resident Canada geese with special methods: to one-half hour after sunset.
Non-toxic shot approved by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is required for all waterfowl hunting in Delaware — no exceptions.
No larger than 10 gauge, plugged to three shells — except with special methods in the September resident goose season.

No hunting from a boat within 1,500 feet of an established blind without the blind owner’s permission. No hunting from a boat within 900 feet of the Delaware River and Bay shore between the Appoquinimink and Smyrna rivers, or within 1,500 feet between the Smyrna and Murderkill rivers, without the landowner’s written permission.
No hunting from a boat, and no floating or fixed blinds, in the Little River where Division of Fish & Wildlife land lies on both sides.

Augustine (Port Penn), Woodland Beach (Route 9 check station) and Little Creek / Ted Harvey blinds are drawn by lottery before shooting time — 2 hours before sunrise, 2½ at Little Creek. Assawoman resident-goose blinds: Mondays and Thursdays in the early season.

Bombay Hook: snow geese Mon, Wed and Fri with the refuge manager’s permission. Prime Hook: September teal blinds by drawing at the refuge check station. Refuges are open to youth only on the Oct 24 and Feb 7 youth days.
October 24, 2026 and February 7, 2027. Youth statewide; veterans and active military on private land only. Hunters under 16 must be supervised by a licensed adult 21 or older.
Leave the head or one fully feathered wing on until you get home, and tag birds left with anyone else (federal rules).

licences.t: Delaware hunting licence (or License Exempt Number)
licences.d: Hunter education is required for anyone born after January 1, 1967.

licences.who: Every migratory bird hunter (not for crows only)
licences.d: Free; a new number each year (valid July 1 – June 30) from de.gov/DigitalDNREC, epermitting.dnrec.delaware.gov or 1-855-335-4868.
Signed in ink across the face, or an e-stamp.

closedNote: Delaware does not publish a statewide list of waters closed to waterfowl. Red areas are DNREC’s closed tracts and safety zones on its wildlife areas.
geometryNote: Geometry: DNREC / Delaware FirstMap (the Teal Zone line — within ~50 m of US 13, DE 1 and US 9 — wildlife-area closures, refuges, boat ramps, DNREC managed lands), USGS NHD (water), USFWS (refuge hunt units; NWI marsh), NOAA CO-OPS (tides), OpenStreetMap (numbered routes, other boat ramps), Census TIGER (state outline, county subdivisions, shared borders). The Teal Zone line across the bay is approximate.
